author: EmuCore - Hub
title: The PlayStation 2 GPU: Graphics Synthesizer (Retro Breakdown)
summary: Frame Rated isolates the PlayStation 2 Graphics Synthesizer and its 4 MB embedded DRAM, then explains how that very small local store interacted with the Emotion Engine and main RDRAM to prioritize bandwidth over modern GPU flexibility.

blocks.text: The eight-minute breakdown keeps its scope deliberately narrow. Chapters define the Graphics Synthesizer, list its principal specifications, focus on the 4 MB eDRAM, and then reconnect the device to the Emotion Engine and main RDRAM. This makes the central trade-off legible: framebuffer space was scarce, yet placing that memory beside the raster hardware provided exceptional local bandwidth. The architecture encouraged developers to manage render targets and texture movement explicitly instead of treating the GPU as a large independent memory domain.

The explanation is introductory and should not be mistaken for a complete GS programming reference. It cites Rodrigo Copetti, PS2DevWiki and period specification material, but the public description does not enumerate every pixel format, bus path or measured bandwidth condition behind the simplified figures. Comparisons with later shader GPUs can also mislead because the GS divided work differently. Use this entry to understand the eDRAM-centered design question, then follow its sources for register-level or cycle-sensitive details.
